components.name: Order Ticket
components.description: Card-stock ticket with a ruled field grid and a dot-matrix clock.
components.css: .ds-ticket{width:320px;background:#f4f6f8;color:#151a2d;border-radius:3px;padding:14px 16px;box-shadow:0 1px 1.5px rgb(21 26 45/.2),0 16px 26px -14px rgb(21 26 45/.55);font-family:var(--font-text,'Barlow',sans-serif)}.ds-ticket header{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;border-bottom:1.5px solid #151a2d;padding-bottom:8px;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.2em}.ds-ticket dl{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:1px;margin:10px 0;background:#c9d1db;border:1px solid #c9d1db}.ds-ticket dl div{background:#f4f6f8;padding:6px 8px}.ds-ticket dt{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.16em;opacity:.7}.ds-ticket dd{margin:0;font-size:22px;font-weight:600}.ds-ticket p{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:baseline;margin:0}.ds-clock{font-family:var(--font-stamp,'DotGothic16',monospace);font-size:17px;letter-spacing:.06em;color:#6b3fa0}.ds-flag{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.2em;opacity:.7}

components.name: Ticket Slot
components.description: Navy file reader with a recessed mouth.
components.css: .ds-slot{width:320px;background:#151a2d;color:#f4f6f8;border-radius:6px;padding:22px 24px;box-shadow:0 2px 3px rgb(21 26 45/.25),0 14px 30px -18px rgb(21 26 45/.9)}.ds-mouth{display:block;height:10px;border-radius:5px;background:color-mix(in oklab,#151a2d,black 55%);box-shadow:inset 0 2px 3px rgb(0 0 0/.6)}.ds-slot:hover .ds-mouth{background:#f2b705}.ds-slot p{margin:18px 0 0;font:600 20px var(--font-text,'Barlow',sans-serif)}

narrative.overview:
Keel is open-outcry pit ephemera: a jacket-gold field, floor-navy ink, and ticket card stock that trades are filed on. Every trade is a ticket that gets filed, stamped and reviewed, and the interface is built from the objects of that ritual: order tickets with ruled field grids, rubber stamps, a navy ticket slot, a trader badge, a punched recap sheet, a rack of cards standing in pockets.

The marketing site is loud and flat. Gold floods the page ground, navy carries every word, and condensed uppercase display type does the shouting. Surfaces are physical paper and metal, so depth is a contact shadow under a card, never a glow. Motion is rare and mechanical: a ticket printing into the stack, a card lifting out of its pocket.
keyCharacteristics: Gold ground, navy ink, stock surfaces; the three never trade roles on the marketing site.
Condensed black uppercase display face against a plain humanist text face.
Buy and sell are always a circled letter, never colour alone; losses print hatched, gains solid.
States are stamps (RULE BROKEN, A+ SETUP) and dashed rules for anything not yet open.
Timestamps are set in a dot-matrix face, in purple, and nowhere else.

rules.name: The Circled Letter Rule
rules.body: Buy blue and sell red never appear alone. They sit in a circled B or S, or in a stamp, so the meaning survives without colour.

rules.name: The Clock Ink Rule
rules.body: Purple is for timestamps and nothing else.

rules.name: The Ground Rule
rules.body: Gold is the ground, navy is the ink. A gold element on gold, or a navy body on navy without the flipped focus ring, is wrong.

rules.name: The Shout Rule
rules.body: Display type is Big Shoulders 900 uppercase, tight leading (0.88-0.9), and used for headlines, buttons, badges and stamps only. Never for running text.

rules.name: The Contact Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every raised thing gets a tight contact shadow plus a soft negative-spread lift, both in navy. No blur-only glows, no hard offset shadows.

dos: Do put gold on the page ground and navy on all ink; keep gold as a button fill only where the surface is navy.
Do pair every buy or sell colour with its circled letter.
Do set every timestamp in the dot-matrix face, purple, in DD MMM HH:MM:SS.
Do show state as a stamp, a hatched loss bar, or a dashed rule.
Do use the two-part navy contact shadow on raised cards.
Do respect reduced motion: the print and pull-from-pocket motions are off, and links underline instead.
donts: Don't put a centred headline over a dark dashboard screenshot; this world refuses that category default.
Don't invent stamps on a visitor's own data: with no rules in the app, tickets print unstamped and Unfiled.
Don't use purple for anything but timestamps.
Don't use blur-only glows or hard offset shadows.
Don't set running text in the display face.
